Exercise A

The Sound Nobody Credited

Read the text carefully, then answer the comprehension questions using the dropdown menus.

Reading Text

Many of the sounds that later defined mainstream pop music were first created by Black musicians in the United States, yet their contributions were often ignored or downplayed for decades. In the 1940s, gospel and blues traditions were combined by artists such as Sister Rosetta Tharpe, whose electric guitar playing is now regarded as an early blueprint for rock'n'roll. During the 1950s, songs written and performed by Black artists like Chuck Berry and Little Richard were frequently re-recorded by white singers, whose versions were promoted more heavily on radio stations that had been segregated by race. As a result, the origins of rock'n'roll were obscured, and its Black pioneers were rarely given the credit or the royalties they deserved.

By the 1960s, a new genre called soul had been developed, blending gospel emotion with rhythm and blues. Record labels such as Motown were founded by Black entrepreneurs, and hits by artists like Aretha Franklin and Marvin Gaye were played across the world. Rhythm and blues was gradually transformed into funk, and its rhythmic techniques were later borrowed by disco and hip hop producers.

Today, it is widely accepted that almost every major pop genre — rock, soul, disco and hip hop — was shaped, directly or indirectly, by Black musical traditions, even though this history was not always taught in schools.

Exercise B

The Passive Voice

Use the passive voice (a form of be + past participle) when the focus is on the action, not on who did it. Choose the correct form of be for each sentence.

Fill in the Gaps

1 Blues and gospel combined by early musicians in the 1940s.

2 Motown founded in 1959 by Berry Gordy.

3 Today, this musical history taught in many schools.

4 By the time rock'n'roll became mainstream, many songs already recorded by Black artists.

5 Aretha Franklin's records still played on the radio today.

6 In the future, more attention probably given to overlooked musicians.

7 The contribution of Black musicians should recognised more often.

8 Soul music being developed throughout the 1960s.
